- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 65–70), model overreacts; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% per day.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid under-shock.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; align forecast with sentiment peaks by +1–2 days in price direction.
